mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series 430d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW 430d engine replacement typically costs between £2,500 and £10,500 for the engine itself, depending on whether you choose used, reconditioned or rebuilt. Specialist fitting adds £780-£1,040 in labour. Used N57D30O1: £2,500-£4,500. Reconditioned B57D30O2: £5,000-£8,000. Rebuilt B57D30O2: £7,000-£10,500.

mainEntity.name: Does the BMW 4 Series 430d have timing chain problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N57 engine in pre-2020 430d models is known for timing chain stretch, typically between 80,000-150,000 miles. The B57 engine in 2020-onwards models is significantly more reliable in this regard. Rattling noise on cold start is the primary warning sign for N57 cars. Preventative N57 chain replacement costs £1,500-£2,500 at a specialist. Ignoring the issue can lead to catastrophic engine failure costing £4,500+.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 430d?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 430d worth over £8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a sound investment that can extend the car's life by 100,000+ miles. For cars under £6,000, a used engine with a preventative chain replacement before fitting is often the most cost-effective route. The 430d's straight-six diesel is highly regarded for its refinement and torque - replacement is often justified. Always factor in fitting costs (£780-£1,040).

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the BMW 430d and 435d engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 3.0-litre straight-six diesels, but the 430d produces 258hp (or 286hp in the B57 generation) while the 435d produces 313hp from a twin-turbo setup. The 435d was replaced by the M440d in the G22 generation. The 430d offers a better balance of performance and fuel economy. 430d: 258-286hp, single or twin-turbo depending on generation. 435d: 313hp, twin-turbo.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 430d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 430d engine replacement takes 12-16 hours of workshop labour due to the straight-six layout. With parts sourcing and scheduling, allow 3-7 working days from order to completion. Supply-only: 2-4 working days for delivery. Supply & fit: 4-7 working days total.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my BMW 430d has the N57 or B57 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The engine change happened with the generation change in 2020. F32/F33/F36 (2013-2020) have the N57D30O1 (258hp). G22/G23/G26 (2020 onwards) have the B57D30O2 or B57D30B (286hp). The easiest way to check is by decoding your VIN. Pre-2020 models have the N57D30O1. 2020-onwards models have the B57D30O2 or B57D30B.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series 430d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 430d launched as the performance diesel flagship of the first-generation 4 Series (F32/F33/F36) in 2013, powered by the smooth and torquey N57 straight-six turbo diesel. In 2020, the second-generation G22 430d received the newer B57 engine with mild-hybrid technology and a power increase to 286hp, cementing the 430d's reputation as the optimal blend of performance and efficiency in the 4 Series diesel line-up.

milestones.description: N57D30O1, 3.0L straight-six turbo diesel, 258hp, launch of F32 430d Coupe

G22 430d launched with B57D30O2, 3.0L straight-six turbo diesel, 286hp, mild-hybrid technology
G23 430d Convertible and G26 430d Gran Coupe join the range
G22 LCI facelift; B57D30B continues with 286hp and Euro 6e emissions compliance

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 430d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 430d is widely regarded as one of the most desirable diesel engines in the 4 Series range, combining effortless torque with refined straight-six smoothness. The N57-powered cars (2013-2020) are generally robust but have known timing chain and turbocharger concerns, while the B57-powered cars (2020 onwards) are more reliable but not immune to DPF and oil leak issues. For 430d owners facing major engine failure, rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why the BMW 4 Series 430d N57 Engine Needs Attention
problems.rootCause: The N57's rear-mounted timing chain design - similar to the N47 - can stretch over time, particularly if oil changes are extended beyond BMW's recommended intervals. Chain stretch causes the cam timing to drift, leading to performance loss and, in severe cases, valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, tensioner; access requires dropping gearbox (rear-mounted chain)
repairOptions.longevity: Best value if caught early - prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has snapped or engine is damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply this UK-wide decision framework to your BMW 4 Series 430d: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: a used engine or preventative chain replacement typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise on cold start from your N57-powered 430d, act immediately - a £1,500-£2,500 preventative chain replacement is far cheaper than a £4,500+ engine replacement. Regular oil changes using the correct BMW Longlife spec are essential for chain longevity.

problems.h4: Turbocharger & DPF Issues - BMW 430d N57 and B57
problems.rootCause: On N57 engines, turbocharger wear (oil supply issues, worn bearings) is a known concern. On B57 engines, DPF clogging from short urban trips is the most common complaint, along with occasional turbocharger wastegate issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Forced regen or chemical DPF clean
repairOptions.longevity: First step for DPF warning light

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and replace turbocharger; check oil supply lines
repairOptions.longevity: N57 turbo failure; do not ignore
Severe cases where turbo failure has contaminated the engine

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a BMW 430d worth £8,000-£15,000, a turbo replacement at a specialist (£1,200-£2,500) is a sensible investment. Full rebuild only makes sense for cars worth over £10,000 or with strong sentimental/commercial value.
problems.recommendation: For N57-powered 430d owners, regular oil changes and allowing the turbo to cool after hard driving will extend turbo life. For B57 owners, ensure regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration - if the warning light appears, a forced regeneration (£250-£500) is far cheaper than a new DPF.
